title: Customer region security questionnaire templates + operator runbook
body:
Purpose:
This doc is a practical bundle for sales, solutions, and onboarding teams: (1) a set of concise security-questionnaire templates focused on region / residency constraints that can be reused in RFPs and pre-sales checks, and (2) an operator-focused runbook describing steps to validate, provision, and evidence a region-constrained tenant deployment.

Scope and assumptions:
- Applies to private and dedicated deployments where customers require geographic constraints on data processing or storage (region lock, country anchoring, or VPC-only routing).
- Assumes customer has signed a basic SOC/contract addendum; this doc helps evaluate feasibility and execute an operational plan.
- Not a legal opinion; contract language should be reviewed by legal for specific jurisdictions.

Quick template: Customer-facing security questionnaire (short form)
Q1. Do you require that customer uploads, user content, and logs remain within a specific country/region? If yes, list the official jurisdiction(s).
A1. We support region constraints via tenant pinning to a region (e.g., eu-west-1) and can restrict control plane operations to approved regions. Please provide exact jurisdiction(s and preferred region codes).

Q2. Which of the following must be region-bound: (a) raw content, (b) derived artifacts (embeddings), (c) logs/telemetry, (d) encryption keys?
A2. We can bind raw content and logs to tenant region. Embeddings/derivatives can be optionally pinned; discuss with solutions engineering. KMS keys can be customer managed in a local region (bring-your-own-key model).

Q3. Do you require on-prem or VPC-only control planes?
A3. Options: hosted control plane with region constraints, private control plane inside customer VPC, or on-prem packaged deployment. Each has different evidence and SLAs — we will recommend based on risk profile.

Q4. Audits and evidence: do you need certificate-level evidence (e.g., signed audit bundle) or operational telemetry for periodic checks? What frequency?
A4. We provide audit bundles (exportable traces + region assertion) on request; monthly/quarterly cadence can be negotiated.

Q5. Acceptable fallback behavior: if region capacity is exhausted, can we route to a nearby region with contractual notice?
A5. Default policy is fail-open to designated fallback regions only if customer explicitly permits in SLA. Otherwise requests will be rejected or queued.

Template: Detailed technical checklist (for Solutions / Eng pre-onboard)
- Jurisdiction mapping: canonical list of ISO region codes + customer legal jurisdiction names. Confirm preferred physical region (cloud provider region id).
- Data types: map each data class to storage and transit controls (user content: pinned; cache/KV: ephemeral pinned TTL; telemetry: hashed-and-aggregated or pinned as required).
- KMS: determine if customer will provide regional CMKs. If yes, capture key ARN and region.
- Control plane: identify whether control-plane metadata (billing, account mgmt) may cross borders; document exception approval.
- Third-party processors: list any connectors (logging, monitoring) that may export data; require region-safe endpoints.

Operator runbook: Provisioning + evidence collection (step-by-step)
1) Intake and verification (SRE + Solutions): confirm questionnaire answers and create onboarding ticket (JIRA key). Attach signed customer statement of region requirements.
2) Create tenant in staging with region attribute set to desired region code. Update tenant metadata with contract clause reference.
3) KMS binding: if customer CMK, configure key policy and test encrypt/decrypt for a sample object in-region. Capture key ARN and KMS audit event.
4) Storage placement: create storage buckets with explicit region constraints; test egress and run cross-region deny rules. Save bucket manifests and IAM policies.
5) Network controls: deploy VPC endpoints, route53 private zones, and verify no NAT egress to non-approved AZs. Collect traceroute evidence and flow logs.
6) Runtime placement: pin worker pools (dedicated pods/GPU nodes) to region. Run sample inference traces and confirm host-region via secure agent fingerprint.
7) Telemetry: configure telemetry pipeline to redact PII and optionally route telemetry to customer-controlled collector in-region. Capture sample telemetry export.
8) Acceptance test: run the residency acceptance test-suite (see test list below) and produce an evidence bundle (signed by operator) containing logs, manifests, and KMS proof.
9) Release to prod. Attach evidence bundle to the tenant record and legal folder.

Residency acceptance test-suite (operator checks)
- Write/read test: Upload a 2MB test blob, confirm physical storage location and reproduce access logs showing region.
- KV cache test: prime KV cache and inspect eviction traces and host placement metadata.
- KMS test: sign a short message via CMK and verify a cryptographically verifiable timestamped audit entry.
- Network test: from an external probe, assert public IPs and traceroute show regional exit nodes within expected ranges.
- Fallback test: simulate region capacity exhaustion and assert behavior matches allowed fallback policy (reject/queued/redirect).

Telemetry keys to capture for audits
- tenant.region_assertion (string)
- operator.evidence_bundle_id (string)
- storage.bucket_region (string)
- kms.key_arn (string)
- runtime.node_region (string)
- event.provenance_hash (hash)
- fallback.decision (allowed|rejected|redirected)

Contract language snippets (developer-friendly, to pass to Legal)
- Data locality clause: "Provider shall ensure Customer Data remains physically stored and processed within [jurisdiction(s)] and shall not transfer, copy, or permit access to Customer Data from any other jurisdiction except with Customer's prior written consent."
- Fallback clause: "Provider may temporarily route requests to [fallback-region(s)] only where Customer has explicitly authorized such routing in writing and where such routing is required for availability reasons; Provider will notify Customer within 24 hours of any such routing event and include evidence."
- Audit bundle SLA: "Provider will produce an audit evidence bundle containing storage manifests, KMS proof, control-plane logs, and network traces within 10 business days of request, subject to reasonable redaction for security-sensitive fields."

SLO / cost implications summary (short bullets)
- No regional fallback: +10-40% operational cost due to dedicated pools and smaller utilization buckets.
- Customer-managed KMS in-region: additional configuration and monitoring but no material runtime latency impact.
- Telemetry pinning: increased storage and retention costs if retained separately per region.

Operational caveats and unresolved questions (for legal/product follow-up)
- Some cloud-managed services (managed metrics collectors, graph services) do not have region-specific tenancy and may require additional connector engineering. Need product decision on allowed exceptions.
- Cross-border subpoenas: how to present evidence when control plane metadata is outside region? Legal to draft standard customer-facing explanation.
- Disaster recovery: recommended DR strategy is cross-jurisdiction warm standby with explicit customer opt-in for failover.

Acceptance criteria for closing onboarding ticket
- Evidence bundle attached and operator-signed.
- Customer confirms acceptance via email for residency test results.
- Billing and SLA document updated with region constraints and fallback policy.

Appendix: helpful commands / search queries (for operators)
- Find tenant region assertion: search telemetry index for tenant.region_assertion:[REGION_CODE]
- Export evidence bundle: /ops/tenants/{tenant_id}/evidence/export?bundle_id={id}
- KMS audit: query CloudKMS -> key ring events between timestamps for key_arn

Notes to self / next steps
- Build a short ticket template for pre-sales to capture exact KMS/region preferences (to reduce back-and-forth).
- Work with infra to create a reusable evidence-bundle generator (zip of manifests + signed metadata).
- Run tabletop with SRE/legal for three representative jurisdictions (EU, UK, Brazil) to validate gaps.

Open links / references
- See CONF-REGION-2821 for canonical jurisdiction mapping and allowed cloud region ids.
- See JIRA-PRIV-6582 for prior onramp for AcmeCorp (example evidence bundle attached).
- PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/private-deploy/pull/812 contains tooling for region-tagging nodes.

End of doc.
